title: Operator-tethered deploy flow notes
summary: Working notes for an operator-driven ‘tethered’ rollout flow that couples traffic ramping to live probe signals and operator checkpoints. Includes wireframe element list, probe mechanics, microcopy drafts, and backlog tasks for implementation and telemetry
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working brainstorm for an operator-tethered rollout UX — a flow that keeps the human operator in the loop while enabling automated, signal-driven ramps and graceful fallback. Goal: give operators a single surface to define the canary or A/B experiment, attach probes (synthetic and real), set safety gates, and optionally enable an automated fallback conductor that can step traffic down or switch routes if key signals degrade.

Why ‘tethered’?
- Tether = operator sets an overall plan and constraints; server-side conductor can act within those constraints.
- Balances autonomy and human oversight for high-risk models or customers with strict SLAs.

High-level flow (operator POV):
1) Create rollout -> choose mode: tethered-canary | tethered-A/B | staged-migration
2) Select baseline (control) and target variant(s) + model versions
3) Define traffic plan: initial fraction, ramp steps, hold durations, max concurrency
4) Attach probes: synthetic probes (predetermined prompts), production probes (sampled requests), latency/cost probes
5) Configure gates: metric thresholds (latency p95 < 180ms), quality thresholds (regression risk < 3% on eval set), error-rate thresholds (5xx < 0.2%)
6) Opt-in: enable automated fallback conductor (policy: soft | strict) and define rollback granularity (reduce by 50% or full revert)
7) Preview simulation -> small-scale dry-run (simulated traffic + probe results)
8) Launch -> operator dashboard and pinned controls (pause, accelerate, rollback)

Wireframe element inventory (for design and engineering):
- Top banner: rollout name, mode, baseline/target tags, status badge (draft / running / paused / degraded / rolled back)
- Traffic ramp builder: horizontal timeline with draggable nodes (0 -> 100%), ability to pin hold points with duration fields; values editable via inline inputs and keyboard
- Probe panel (collapsible): list of probes, each with type icon (synth / prod-sample / latency / cost), measurement window, sample size, last-run summary, attach/remove actions
- Gate configuration sheet: key metrics table (metric name, operator-set threshold, evaluation window, comparison method), ability to link to an eval set or upload a prompt set
- Conductor policy modal: radio options (manual-only, soft-auto, strict-auto). Soft-auto = auto-step-down by fraction and alert ops; strict-auto = immediate revert to baseline and create incident
- Quick-controls ribbon: Pause (sticky), Accelerate (opens confirm), Rollback (confirm with impact estimate), Simulate (runs preview)
- Audit timeline: display events with actor (operator/system), metric deltas, and links to sample requests or probe runs
- ‘What-if’ simulator: dropdown to pick a metric to degrade (latency/quality/error) and view projected traffic and cost outcomes if that metric crosses threshold
- Safety summary card: shows current health (green/amber/red), reason, and recommended action (e.g., reduce ramp, increase probe frequency)

Probe mechanics notes:
- Synthetic probes: operator provides small prompt set per workload; system will run X queries / minute; results evaluated against expected golden outputs (or fuzzy scoring). Use for deterministic regression checks and hallucination detection.
- Production probes: lightweight sampling of real traffic (strip PII, sampled at 0.1%) with privacy-preserving anonymization. Useful for emergent failure modes not captured by synthetic prompts.
- Lagged evaluation: allow probes to run in parallel and compute windowed statistics (1m, 5m, 15m). Conductor only uses stable windows (e.g., >3m) for automated actions.

Fallback conductor policy examples (drafts for engineering):
- Soft-auto example: if quality_score_drop > 4% over two consecutive 5m windows OR error_rate > 1% -> reduce target traffic by 50% and notify operator; continue monitoring and re-evaluate in 10m
- Strict-auto example: if latency_p95 > 250ms OR 5xx_rate > 2% for 2 consecutive windows -> immediate rollback to baseline and open incident; pin rollback reason in audit timeline

Microcopy drafts (inline help & operator prompts):
- Rollout name placeholder: “eg. tethered-sales-ltr-v2”
- Traffic ramp slider tooltip: “Drag to set the max percent of production traffic for this variant. Holds will pause the ramp until checkpoints pass.”
- Probe description: “Synthetic probes run pre-defined prompts to detect regressions and hallucinations. Use small focused sets for quicker feedback.”
- Conductor soft-auto tooltip: “Can automatically reduce traffic when signals degrade; will create an alert and wait for operator confirmation before full revert.”

Backlog (implementation & grooming items):
- INF-1423: Backend: probe runner v1 (synthetic + prod sampling) + scoring hooks (owner: Li Wei)
- INF-1499: UI: ramp builder interaction patterns and accessibility (owner: Jonah Patel)
- INF-1507: Telemetry: rollout-level metrics and KPI dashboard (owner: María González)
- INF-1518: Privacy review: design prod sampling sanitizer and compliance checklist (collab: security)
- UX-qa: microcopy pass + localization impact analysis
- E2E: simulate degraded metric scenarios for soft/strict conductor policies

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (to capture in product meeting):
- How to express multi-variant A/B decisions when multiple metrics trade off (cost vs quality)? Need a prioritized metric list or composite score?
- When soft-auto triggers a partial step-down, should we lock accelerated operator changes until a cooldown expires?
- Probe sampling rates — default and per-tenant overrides to balance cost and signal fidelity
- Audit signal provenance: how much context to keep (full sample vs snippet). Security will push minimal snippets.

Operator checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Define golden probe set and run local simulation
- [ ] Set SLO-driven gates and reasonable hold durations (start conservative)
- [ ] Fill incident contacts and Slack webhook for automatic alerts
- [ ] Confirm privacy sanitizer policy for prod probes

Notes on UX flows for edge cases:
- Operator pauses -> show clear ‘paused by’ actor + resume button; do not allow auto-conductor to resume without explicit operator consent unless operator previously opted-in to auto-resume
- Partial rollback with multi-variant experiments -> allow operator to shift traffic between variants atomically (button: ‘re-balance to baseline/variant X’) and show impact estimate
- Network flaps / infra noise -> conductor should ignore single-window spikes; require 2+ consecutive windows to avoid flip-flopping

Prototype & next steps:
- High-fidelity prototype (Figma): ramp builder + probe panel + quick-controls ribbon (assigned to Jonah)
- Backend contract: probe result shape, conductor policy API, audit event format (assigned to Li)
- Teardown plan: doc example of a rollback incident (what operator sees, what telemetry is captured) for postmortem templates

Appendix: sample prompts for synthetic probes (starter kit)
- “Summarize the following invoice in 2 bullet points.” (checks structured output and hallucination)
- “Rewrite this product blurb to emphasize privacy features.” (checks style and instruction following)
- “Given user input ‘How do I reset my password?’, produce step-by-step instructions.” (checks safety & policy tokens)

This doc is intentionally informal — capture ideas and tradeoffs. Please add inline comments and tag which items you want picked up for grooming.

- Flag anything that would cause regulatory friction for prod sampling
- Add UX edge-cases we missed (multi-region rollouts, cross-tenant account policies)
